items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee mentions Jay McShann only in the context of other people (John Jackson, Taswell Baird) having been in Jay McShann's band. There is no direct interaction or personal relationship described between the interviewee (John Malachi) and Jay McShann.

ctx.x: happen too often. So he decided he would leave the band. That's when he sent for and got an old school-mate of his, a fellow that he'd grown up with and had played in Jay McShann's band with him, a fellow named John Jackson, a very good saxophone player. John was a quiet sort of a fellow, and I think labored in the shadow of Charlie Parker. He always felt a little inferior to Charlie, and he was a little insecure about what he was doing. But everybody loved the way John played, and he was a very good first alto…

One of the things that I remember about this genius of Charlie Parker was.... Back to the time when we first rehearsed the band in New York, at our very first rehearsal, these arrangements we played, the eight arrangements that we played... And they had a good sound and everything, and the band was sounding good.
